title.zh: 卷十五 列傳第九 謝朏 弟子覽
title.raw: 卷十五 列傳第九 謝朏 弟子覽 Volume 15: Xie Fei; Xie Lan

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第十五 列傳第九

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 15, Biographies 9
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 15, Biographies 9

sentences.zh: 謝朏 弟子覽

translations.literal: Xie Fei; his nephew Lan
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fei; his nephew Lan

sentences.zh: 謝朏字敬沖，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Xie Fei, styled Jingchong, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fei, styled Jingchong, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖弘微，宋太常卿，父莊，右光祿大夫，並有名前代。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hongwei was Song Grand Minister of Ceremonies; his father Zhuang was Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—both were famed in earlier generations.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hongwei had been Song grand minister of ceremonies; his father Zhuang, right grand master of splendid happiness—both were celebrated in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 朏幼聰慧，莊器之，常置左右。

translations.literal: Fei was clever from childhood; Zhuang treasured him and kept him always at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was bright as a boy; Zhuang prized him and never let him leave his side.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，能屬文。

translations.literal: At ten he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could write finished prose.

sentences.zh: 莊游土山賦詩，使朏命篇，朏攬筆便就。

translations.literal: When Zhuang visited Mount Tu and composed poetry, he set Fei a topic; Fei took up the brush and finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang toured Mount Tu and wrote verse, he gave Fei the theme; Fei took brush and finished on the spot.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王景文謂莊曰：「賢子足稱神童，復爲後來特達。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Langye, Wang Jingwen, said to Zhuang: "Your worthy son deserves the name wonder child; he will be a singular talent yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Langye, Wang Jingwen, told Zhuang, "Your worthy son may be called a wonder child—a singular talent still to come.

sentences.zh: 」莊笑，因撫朏背曰：「真吾家千金。

translations.literal: " Zhuang laughed, stroked Fei's back, and said: "Truly the thousand gold of our house."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuang laughed, stroked Fei's back, and said, "Truly the thousand gold of our house."

sentences.zh: 」孝武帝游姑孰，勑莊攜朏從駕，詔使爲《洞井贊》，於坐奏之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu toured Gudu; he ordered Zhuang to bring Fei in the entourage and commanded him to compose "Ode on the Cave Well," which he presented in the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu toured Gudu, ordered Zhuang to bring Fei in the train, and commanded an "Ode on the Cave Well," which Fei presented in the hall.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「雖小，奇童也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Small though he is, a wonder child."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Small as he is, a wonder child."

sentences.zh: 起家撫軍法曹行參軍，遷太子舍人，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He began office as Acting Staff Officer in the Pacifying Army, moved to Crown Prince Attendant, and left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He began as pacifying-army acting staff officer, became crown prince attendant, and left office for his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，復爲舍人，歷中書郎，衛將軍袁粲長史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he again became attendant, served as Palace Secretariat Gentleman and chief of staff to Guard General Yuan Can.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was again attendant, then palace secretariat gentleman and chief of staff to guard general Yuan Can.

sentences.zh: 粲性簡峻，罕通賓客，時人方之李膺。

translations.literal: Can was stern and sparing with guests; men of the time compared him to Li Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Can was austere and rarely received guests; contemporaries likened him to Li Ying.

sentences.zh: 朏謁旣退，粲曰：「謝令不死。

translations.literal: After Fei's audience withdrew, Can said, "Commander Xie does not die."
translations.idiomatic: When Fei's visit ended, Can said, "Commander Xie is not dead."

sentences.zh: 」尋遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Attendant and Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose to attendant and yellow gate gentleman.

sentences.zh: 出爲臨川內史，以賄見劾，案經袁粲，粲寢之。

translations.literal: He went out as Interior Magistrate of Linchuan; accused of bribery, the case reached Yuan Can, who suppressed it.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Linchuan interior magistrate; bribery charges reached Yuan Can, who buried the case.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝爲驃騎將軍輔政，選朏爲長史，勑與河南褚炫、濟陽江斅、彭城劉俁俱入侍宋帝，時號爲天子四友。

translations.literal: Qi Emperor Gao, as Rapid Cavalry General assisting government, chose Fei as chief of staff and ordered him with Chu Xuan of Henan, Jiang Jiao of Jiyang, and Liu Hou of Pengcheng to attend the Song emperor—they were called the Son of Heaven's Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Emperor Gao, as regent rapid-cavalry general, made Fei his chief of staff and sent him with Chu Xuan of Henan, Jiang Jiao of Jiyang, and Liu Hou of Pengcheng to attend the Song emperor—men called them the Son of Heaven's Four Friends.

sentences.zh: 續拜侍中，並掌中書、散騎二省詔冊。

translations.literal: He was further made Attendant-in-Ordinary, jointly managing the edicts of the Secretariat and Scattered Cavalry bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made attendant-in-ordinary and jointly managed secretariat and scattered-cavalry edicts.

sentences.zh: 高帝進太尉，又以朏爲長史，帶南東海太守。

translations.literal: When Gao advanced to Grand Marshal, he again made Fei chief of staff with concurrent Southern Donghai prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao became grand marshal, he again made Fei chief of staff with Southern Donghai prefect in addition.

sentences.zh: 高帝方圖禪代，思佐命之臣，以朏有重名，深所欽屬。

translations.literal: Gao was plotting to seize the throne and sought ministers who would aid the mandate; because Fei had great renown, he deeply admired and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was plotting the abdication and wanted ministers to crown the change; Fei's great name made Gao admire and lean on him.

sentences.zh: 論魏、晉故事，因曰：「晉革命時事久兆，石苞不早勸晉文，死方慟哭，方之馮異，非知機也。

translations.literal: Discussing Wei and Jin precedents, he said: "When Jin changed the mandate the signs were long visible; Shi Bao did not early urge Wen of Jin—he only wailed at death. Compared to Feng Yi, that is not knowing the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Discussing Wei and Jin precedents, he said, "When Jin took the mandate the omen was old; Shi Bao did not urge Wen of Jin in time—he wept only at death. Set beside Feng Yi, that is not reading the hour.

sentences.zh: 」朏答曰：「昔魏臣有勸魏武卽帝位者，魏武曰：『如有用我，其爲周文王乎！

translations.literal: " Fei answered: "Of old among Wei ministers some urged Martial Emperor of Wei to take the throne; Martial Emperor said, 'If heaven would use me, would I not be like King Wen of Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: " Fei answered, "Of old a Wei minister urged Martial Emperor of Wei to take the throne; Martial Emperor said, 'If Heaven would use me, would I not be King Wen of Zhou!

sentences.zh: 』晉文世事魏氏，將必身終北面；

translations.literal: ' Wen of Jin served the house of Wei and was bound to die facing north;
translations.idiomatic: ' Wen of Jin served the house of Wei and was bound to end his days facing north;

sentences.zh: 假使魏早依唐虞故事，亦當三讓彌高。

translations.literal: had Wei early followed the model of Yao and Shun, he would still have thrice yielded to the highest degree.
translations.idiomatic: had Wei early followed Yao and Shun, he would still have yielded three times to the utmost height.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 更引王儉爲左長史，以朏侍中，領秘書監。

translations.literal: He brought in Wang Jian as left chief of staff and kept Fei as attendant-in-ordinary with charge of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Wang Jian as left chief of staff and kept Fei as attendant-in-ordinary directing the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 及齊受禪，朏當日在直，百僚陪位，侍中當解璽，朏佯不知，曰：「有何公事？

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Fei was on duty that day; all officials took their places; the attendant-in-ordinary should unseal the imperial seal. Fei pretended not to know and said, "What business is there?
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, Fei was on duty; the hundred officials took their stations; the attendant-in-ordinary should unseal the seal. Fei played ignorant and said, "What business is there?

sentences.zh: 」傳詔云：「解璽授齊王。

translations.literal: " The relay edict said, "Unseal and transfer to the King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " The relay edict said, "Unseal and hand it to the King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 」朏曰：「齊自應有侍中。

translations.literal: " Fei said, "Qi surely has its own attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei said, "Qi ought to have its own attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 」乃引枕臥。

translations.literal: " He took a pillow and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: " He fetched a pillow and lay down.

sentences.zh: 傳詔懼，乃使稱疾，欲取兼人。

translations.literal: The relay messenger was afraid; they had him feign illness to fetch a substitute.
translations.idiomatic: The relay messenger panicked and had him claim illness to bring in a stand-in.

sentences.zh: 朏曰：「我無疾，何所道。

translations.literal: Fei said, "I have no illness; what is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: Fei said, "I am not ill; what is there to report?

sentences.zh: 」遂朝服，步出東掖門，乃得車，仍還宅。

translations.literal: " He put on court dress, walked out the eastern side gate, got a carriage, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: " He dressed in court robes, walked out the eastern side gate, found a carriage, and went home.

sentences.zh: 是日遂以王儉爲侍中解璽。

translations.literal: That day Wang Jian was made attendant-in-ordinary to unseal the seal.
translations.idiomatic: That day Wang Jian was made attendant-in-ordinary to unseal the seal.

sentences.zh: 旣而武帝言於高帝，請誅朏。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Wu of Qi spoke to Gao, asking to execute Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Wu of Qi spoke to Gao and asked to kill Fei.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「殺之則遂成其名，正應容之度外耳。

translations.literal: Gao said, "Kill him and his name is made; better to tolerate him beyond the pale."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "Kill him and you make his name; better to spare him beyond the pale."

sentences.zh: 」遂廢于家。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and kept at home.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，起家拜通直散騎常侍，累遷侍中，領國子博士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he began as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, rose through offices to Attendant-in-Ordinary with charge as National University Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming's first year he began as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary, rose to attendant-in-ordinary, and led the national university as erudite.

sentences.zh: 五年，出爲冠軍將軍、義興太守，加秩中二千石。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out as Champion General and Yixing prefect, with rank of middle two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he went out as champion general and Yixing prefect with middle two-thousand-bushel rank.

sentences.zh: 在郡不省雜事，悉付綱紀，曰：「吾不能作主者吏，但能作太守耳。

translations.literal: In the commandery he did not oversee miscellaneous affairs, giving all to the clerks, and said, "I cannot be the clerk who runs things; I can only be the prefect."
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he ignored routine business and gave it all to clerks, saying, "I cannot be the clerk in charge—I can only be the prefect."

sentences.zh: 」視事三年，徵都官尚書、中書令。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was recalled as Director of the Court Offices and Palace Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was recalled as director of the court offices and palace secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，復爲侍中，領新安王師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was again Attendant-in-Ordinary, leading tutor to the Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang's first year he was again attendant-in-ordinary, leading tutor to the prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 未拜，固求外出。

translations.literal: Before taking the appointment he firmly sought to go out on assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Before investiture he begged hard to go out on assignment.

sentences.zh: 仍爲征虜將軍、吳興太守，受召便述職。

translations.literal: He was still made General Who Punishes Barbarians and Wu-xing prefect; on summons he took office at once.
translations.idiomatic: He was still made general who punishes barbarians and Wu-xing prefect; summoned, he took office at once.

sentences.zh: 時明帝謀入嗣位，朝之舊臣皆引參謀策。

translations.literal: Mingdi was then plotting succession to the throne; old ministers of the court were all drawn into counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi was then plotting to enter the succession; old courtiers were all drawn into counsel.

sentences.zh: 朏內圖止足，且實避事。

translations.literal: Fei inwardly sought sufficiency and truly wished to avoid affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fei inwardly sought enough and truly meant to avoid affairs.

sentences.zh: 弟𤅢，時爲吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His brother Yin was then Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yin was then director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 朏至郡，致𤅢數斛酒，遺書曰：「可力飲此，勿豫人事。

translations.literal: Arriving at the commandery, he sent Yin several piculs of wine with a letter that said, "Drink this with all your strength; do not meddle in human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: At the commandery he sent Yin several piculs of wine with a letter: "Drink this hard; keep out of men's business."

sentences.zh: 」朏居郡每不治，而常務聚斂，衆頗譏之，亦不屑也。

translations.literal: In the commandery Fei rarely governed yet constantly pursued levies; many criticized him, and he did not care.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery Fei seldom governed yet always gathered revenue; many mocked him, and he did not care.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，詔徵爲侍中、中書令，遂抗表不應召。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu an edict summoned him as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Secretariat Director; he submitted a memorial refusing the summons.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu's fourth year an edict summoned him as attendant-in-ordinary and palace secretariat director; he memorialized and refused.

sentences.zh: 遣諸子還京師，獨與母留，築室郡之西郭。

translations.literal: He sent his sons back to the capital but stayed alone with his mother, building a house west of the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his sons to the capital, stayed alone with his mother, and built a house west of the commandery wall.

sentences.zh: 明帝下詔曰：「夫超然榮觀，風流自遠；

translations.literal: Mingdi issued an edict: "One who stands apart from glory views the world from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi issued an edict: "To stand beyond glory is to see the world from far off;

sentences.zh: 蹈彼幽人，英華罕值。

translations.literal: one who treads the hermit's path is rarely met in full flower.
translations.idiomatic: to walk the hermit's way is to bloom in solitude.

sentences.zh: 故長揖楚相，見稱南國；

translations.literal: Hence Chang Fu's long bow to the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;
translations.idiomatic: hence the long bow of the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;

sentences.zh: 高謝漢臣，取貴良史。

translations.literal: the Han worthy's high refusal won honor from fine historians.
translations.idiomatic: the Han worthy's lofty refusal won honor from fine historians.

sentences.zh: 新除侍中、中書令朏，早藉羽儀，夙標清尚，登朝樹績，出守馳聲。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Secretariat Director Fei long bore the court insignia and from youth bore a pure reputation; in court he built merit, going out he made his name heard.
translations.idiomatic: The newly appointed attendant-in-ordinary and palace secretariat director Fei long wore court insignia and from youth bore a clear name; in court he built merit, abroad he made his name heard.

sentences.zh: 遂斂跡康衢，拂衣林沚，抱箕潁之餘芳，甘憔悴而無悶。

translations.literal: Then he gathered his steps from the broad highway and shook the dust from his forest robes, embracing the lingering fragrance of Jiqian and Ying, content in lean exile without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Then he gathered his steps from the broad highway and shook dust from forest robes, keeping the after-scent of Jiqian and Ying, glad in lean exile without regret.

sentences.zh: 撫事懷人，載留欽想。

translations.literal: Hearing of his deeds one keeps him in honored thought.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his story, one keeps him in honored thought.

sentences.zh: 宜加優禮，用旌素概。

translations.literal: He should receive added courtesy to mark his plain integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Let added courtesy mark his plain integrity.

sentences.zh: 可賜床帳褥席，俸以卿祿，常出在所。

translations.literal: Grant bed curtains and padded mats, salary at minister rank, always provided at his dwelling."
translations.idiomatic: Grant bed curtains and padded mats, salary at minister rank, always sent to his dwelling."

sentences.zh: 」時國子祭酒廬江何胤亦抗表還會稽。

translations.literal: At that time National University Chancellor He Yin of Lujiang also submitted a memorial to return to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: At that time national university chancellor He Yin of Lujiang also memorialized to return to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，詔徵朏爲散騎常侍、中書監，胤爲散騎常侍、太常卿，並不屈。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan an edict summoned Fei as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary and Imperial Library Director, and Yin as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Minister of Ceremonies—neither yielded.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan's second year an edict summoned Fei as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary and imperial library director, and Yin as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary and grand minister of ceremonies—neither came.

sentences.zh: 三年，又詔徵朏爲侍中、太子少傅，胤散騎常侍、太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the third year another edict summoned Fei as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, and Yin as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary and Crown Prince Household Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year another edict summoned Fei as attendant-in-ordinary and junior tutor to the crown prince, and Yin as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary and crown prince household superintendent.

sentences.zh: 時東昏皆下在所，使迫遣之，值義師已近，故並得不到。

translations.literal: By then Emperor Donghun was under house arrest at the palace; messengers were sent to hurry them, but the righteous army was already near, so neither could be fetched.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Donghun was confined at the palace; messengers were sent to hurry them, but the righteous army was already near, so neither was reached.

sentences.zh: 及高祖平京邑，進位相國，表請朏、胤曰：「夫窮則獨善，達以兼濟。

translations.literal: When Gaozu pacified the capital and advanced to Chancellor of State, he memorialized requesting Fei and Yin, saying: "When poor, one keeps to oneself; when risen, one aids all.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu pacified the capital and advanced to chancellor of state, he memorialized for Fei and Yin, saying, "In want one keeps to oneself; risen, one aids all.

sentences.zh: 雖出處之道，其揆不同，用舍惟時，賢哲是蹈。

translations.literal: Though the way of going out and staying in differs in measure, timing decides employment, and the wise tread accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Though the way of going out and staying in differs in measure, use and refusal follow the hour, and the wise tread it.

sentences.zh: 前新除侍中、太子少傅朏，前新除散騎常侍、太子詹事、都亭侯胤，羽儀世胄，徽猷冠冕，道業德聲，康濟雅俗。

translations.literal: The former newly appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Fei, and the former newly appointed Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, Crown Prince Household Superintendent, and Marquis of Duting Yin—both are feathered scions of noble houses, emblem bearers of the crown, their conduct and fame a balm to refined custom.
translations.idiomatic: The former newly appointed attendant-in-ordinary and junior tutor to the crown prince Fei, and the former newly appointed regular palace attendant-in-ordinary, crown prince household superintendent, and marquis of Duting Yin—feathered heirs of noble lines, emblem bearers of the crown, conduct and fame a balm to refined custom.

sentences.zh: 昔居朝列，素無宦情，賓客簡通，公卿罕預，簪紱未褫，而風塵擺落。

translations.literal: In former days at court they were without appetite for office; guests were few and grandees rarely met; their rank sashes were not yet removed when the dust of turmoil brushed them off.
translations.idiomatic: In former days at court they had no taste for office; guests were few and grandees rarely met; rank sashes were not yet off when turmoil's dust brushed them away.

sentences.zh: 且文宗儒肆，互居其長；

translations.literal: One was master of the Confucian grove;
translations.idiomatic: One was master of the Confucian grove;

sentences.zh: 清規雅裁，兼擅其美。

translations.literal: the other combined elegant rule with refined judgment.
translations.idiomatic: the other combined elegant rule with refined judgment.

sentences.zh: 並達照深識，預睹亂萌，見庸質之如初，知貽厥之無寄。

translations.literal: Each saw deep and judged early, foresaw the sprouting chaos, knew vulgar quality at first glance, and knew there was nothing to pass on to heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Each saw deep and judged early, foresaw chaos sprouting, knew vulgar quality at first glance, and knew there was nothing to pass to heirs.

sentences.zh: 拂衣東山，眇絕塵軌。

translations.literal: They shook out their robes on the eastern hills and cut the dust from their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: They shook out robes on the eastern hills and cut dust from their tracks.

sentences.zh: 雖解組昌運，實避昏時。

translations.literal: Though they surrendered their seals in a prosperous age, they truly fled a benighted time.
translations.idiomatic: Though they surrendered seals in a prosperous age, they truly fled a benighted time.

sentences.zh: 家膺鼎食，而甘茲橡艾；

translations.literal: Families that ate from the tripod yet savored oak and mugwort;
translations.idiomatic: Families that ate from the tripod yet savored oak and mugwort;

sentences.zh: 世襲青紫，而安此懸鶉。

translations.literal: lineages that inherited purple and blue yet rested easy as hanging quail.
translations.idiomatic: lineages that inherited purple and blue yet rested easy as hanging quail.

sentences.zh: 自澆風肇扇，用南成俗，淳流素軌，餘烈頗存。

translations.literal: Since the shallow wind first stirred, the south became custom; the pure current and plain track still had much force left.
translations.idiomatic: Since the shallow wind first stirred, the south became custom; the pure current and plain track still had force left.

sentences.zh: 誰其激貪，功歸有道，康俗振民，朝野一致。

translations.literal: Who stirs against greed—the merit returns to the Way; who revives custom and lifts the people makes court and countryside one.
translations.idiomatic: Who stirs against greed—the merit returns to the Way; who revives custom and lifts the people makes court and countryside one.

sentences.zh: 雖在江海，而勳同魏闕。

translations.literal: Though they dwelt by rivers and sea, their merit matched the Wei audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Though they dwelt by rivers and sea, their merit matched the Wei audience hall.

sentences.zh: 今泰運甫開，賤貧爲恥；

translations.literal: Now the great fortune is just opening; to be poor and low is shame;
translations.idiomatic: Now the great fortune is just opening; to be poor and low is shame;

sentences.zh: 況乎久蘊瑚璉，暫厭承明，而可得求志海隅，永追松子。

translations.literal: how much more those who long harbored jade and ritual vessels, who for a time loathed the Bright Hall—can they seek their will at the sea's edge and forever chase Master Chizi?
translations.idiomatic: how much more those who long harbored jade and ritual vessels, who for a time loathed the Bright Hall—can they seek their will at the sea's edge and forever chase Master Chizi?

sentences.zh: 臣負荷殊重，參贊萬機，寔賴羣才，共成棟幹。

translations.literal: Your servant bears a singular burden and shares in the myriad affairs of state; he truly relies on many talents to raise the roof beam together.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant bears a singular burden and shares in the myriad affairs of state; he truly relies on many talents to raise the roof beam together.

sentences.zh: 思挹清源，取鏡止水。

translations.literal: He wishes to draw from the clear spring and take the still water as mirror.
translations.idiomatic: He wishes to draw from the clear spring and take still water as mirror.

sentences.zh: 愚欲屈居僚首，朝夕諮諏，庶足以翼宣寡薄，式是王度。

translations.literal: He wishes to bend them to the first rank among his staff, to consult morning and evening, that they may help spread his thin virtue and shape the kingly measure.
translations.idiomatic: He wishes to bend them to the first rank among his staff, to consult morning and evening, that they may help spread his thin virtue and shape the kingly measure.

sentences.zh: 請並補臣府軍諮祭酒，朏加後將軍。

translations.literal: Request that both be appointed military affairs adviser and libation officer in your servant's chancellery, with Fei additionally made Rear General."
translations.idiomatic: Request that both be appointed military affairs adviser and libation officer in your servant's chancellery, with Fei additionally made rear general."

sentences.zh: 」並不至。

translations.literal: Neither came.
translations.idiomatic: Neither came.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，徵朏爲侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，胤散騎常侍、特進、右光祿大夫，又並不屈。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Fei was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Bearer of the Golden Halberd with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies; Yin was summoned as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, Special Grandee, and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—they again both refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Fei was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, left grand master of splendid happiness, and bearer of the golden halberd with protocol equal to the three excellencies; Yin as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary, special grandee, and right grand master of splendid happiness—they again both refused.

sentences.zh: 仍遣領軍司馬王果宣旨敦譬。

translations.literal: A messenger from the palace guard staff officer Wang Guo was again sent to convey the edict with earnest persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guard staff officer Wang Guo was again sent to convey the edict with earnest persuasion.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，朏輕舟出，詣闕自陳。

translations.literal: The next year in the sixth month Fei took a light boat and came to the palace to report in person.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the sixth month, Fei took a light boat and came to the palace to report in person.

sentences.zh: 旣至，詔以爲侍中、司徒、尚書令。

translations.literal: On arrival an edict made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Marshal, and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival an edict made him attendant-in-ordinary, grand marshal, and director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 朏辭腳疾不堪拜謁，乃角巾肩輿，詣雲龍門謝。

translations.literal: Fei pleaded that leg ailment prevented kneeling in audience; he wore kerchief and shoulder carriage and came to Cloud Dragon Gate to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Fei pleaded leg ailment and could not kneel in audience; he wore kerchief and rode a shoulder carriage to Cloud Dragon Gate to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 詔見於華林園，乘小車就席。

translations.literal: An edict received him in Hualin Garden; he sat in a small carriage at the mat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict received him in Hualin Garden; he sat in a small carriage at the mat.

sentences.zh: 明旦，輿駕出幸朏宅，醼語盡歡。

translations.literal: Next morning the imperial carriage went out to visit Fei's house; they feasted and talked in full joy.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning the imperial carriage visited Fei's house; they feasted and talked in full joy.

sentences.zh: 朏固陳本志，不許；

translations.literal: Fei firmly stated his original intent; the emperor would not allow it;
translations.idiomatic: Fei firmly stated his original intent; the emperor would not allow it;

sentences.zh: 因請自還東迎母，乃許之。

translations.literal: he then asked to go east himself to fetch his mother, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: he then asked to go east himself to fetch his mother, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 臨發，輿駕復臨幸，賦詩餞別。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure the imperial carriage again came to visit, composing poetry to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure the imperial carriage again visited, composing poetry to see him off.

sentences.zh: 王人送迎，相望於道。

translations.literal: Court envoys went out and escorted him back—one party's procession met the other's on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Court envoys went out and escorted him back—processions met on the road.

sentences.zh: 到京師，勑材官起府於舊宅，高祖臨軒，遣謁者於府拜授，詔停諸公事及朔望朝謁。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital, an order had the materiel office raise a mansion at his old residence; the emperor came to the front hall and sent an usher to the mansion to invest him with office; an edict suspended all public business and the new-moon and full-moon audiences.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital, an order had the materiel office raise a mansion at his old residence; the emperor came to the front hall and sent an usher to the mansion to invest him; an edict suspended all public business and new-moon and full-moon audiences.

sentences.zh: 子諼，官至司徒右長史，坐殺牛免官，卒於家。

translations.literal: His son Xuan rose to Right Chief of Staff of the Grand Marshal; he was dismissed from office for killing an ox and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan rose to right chief of staff of the grand marshal; dismissed for killing an ox, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 次子篹，頗有文才，仕至晉安太守，卒官。

translations.literal: His second son Sao had considerable literary talent, served to Jin'an prefect, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Sao had considerable literary gift, served to Jin'an prefect, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 覽爲人美風神，善辭令，高祖深器之。

translations.literal: Lan was a man of fine bearing and spirit, skilled in eloquence; Gaozu deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Lan had a handsome presence and gift for speech; the Founding Emperor prized him greatly.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍座，受敕與侍中王暕爲詩答贈。

translations.literal: Once while attending in his seat, he received an edict to compose an answering poem with Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Jian in reply to an exchange of gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Once in attendance he was ordered, with Attendant Wang Jian, to compose answering verse for a gift exchange.

sentences.zh: 其文甚工。

translations.literal: His writing was very skilled.
translations.idiomatic: The piece was finely wrought.

sentences.zh: 高祖善之，仍使重作，復合旨。

translations.literal: Gaozu was pleased and had him write again; it again matched intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and asked for another; again it fit the wish.

sentences.zh: 乃賜詩云：「雙文旣後進，二少實名家；

translations.literal: Then he bestowed a poem that read: "Both Wen are rising talents; the two youths are truly famous houses;
translations.idiomatic: He granted a poem: "Twin Wen are latecomers yet rising; both young men are true great clans;

sentences.zh: 豈伊止棟隆，信乃俱國華。

translations.literal: how could they merely bear up the ridgepole's height? Truly both are the state's finest flowers."
translations.idiomatic: could they only lift the ridgebeam? Surely both are the realm's finest blossoms."

sentences.zh: 」以母憂去職。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left his post for mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除中庶子，又掌吏部郎事，尋除吏部郎，遷侍中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent, also handled the Bureau Director of Personnel's affairs, soon made Bureau Director, then promoted Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became heir-apparent companion, handled Personnel bureau director duties, soon became director, then attendant.

sentences.zh: 覽頗樂酒，因醼席與散騎常侍蕭琛辭相詆毀，爲有司所奏。

translations.literal: Lan was quite fond of wine; at a banquet with Regular Attendant of the Writes-on-the-Fast Xiao Chen they exchanged abusive words and were reported by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Lan loved wine; at a feast he and Regular Attendant Xiao Chen traded insults, and the authorities memorialized against them.

sentences.zh: 高祖以覽年少不直，出爲中權長史。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because Lan was young and not straightforward, sent him out as Chief Clerk of the Central Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, holding Lan young and not upright, sent him out as Central Guards chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 頃之，敕掌東宮管記，遷明威將軍、新安太守。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he was ordered to manage Eastern Palace records, promoted General of Bright Might and Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to keep Eastern Palace records, promoted Bright Might general and Xin'an administrator.

sentences.zh: 九年夏，山賊吳承伯破宣城郡，餘黨散入新安，叛吏鮑敘等與合，攻沒黟、歙諸縣，進兵擊覽。

translations.literal: In summer of year nine, mountain bandit Wu Chengbo smashed Xuancheng commandery; remnants scattered into Xin'an; rebel clerk Bao Xu and others joined them, seized Yi and She counties, and advanced to attack Lan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year's summer, bandit Wu Chengbo broke Xuancheng; survivors fled into Xin'an; rebel clerks Bao Xu and others joined, took Yi and She, and marched on Lan.

sentences.zh: 覽遣郡丞周興嗣于錦沙立塢拒戰，不敵，遂棄郡奔會稽。

translations.literal: Lan sent Commandery Assistant Zhou Xingsi to build a stockade at Jinsha to resist; they were no match and he abandoned the commandery and fled to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Lan sent assistant Zhou Xingsi to fortify Jinsha and fight; defeated, he abandoned the commandery and fled to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 臺軍平山寇，覽復還郡，左遷司徒諮議參軍、仁威長史、行南徐州事，五兵尚書。

translations.literal: When court troops pacified the mountain raiders, Lan returned to the commandery, then was demoted to Adviser of the Minister of the Masters of Works, Chief Clerk of Humaneness and Might, acting South Xuzhou affairs, and Minister of the Five Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: When the army pacified the bandits, Lan returned; then he was demoted to Masters of Works adviser, Humaneness and Might chief clerk, acting South Xuzhou, and Five Armaments minister.

sentences.zh: 尋遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 覽自祖至孫，三世居選部，當世以爲榮。

translations.literal: From grandfather to grandson, Lan's line held the selection bureau three generations—a glory of the age.
translations.idiomatic: From grandfather through grandson, three generations held the personnel bureau—the age took it for honor.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，出爲吳興太守。

translations.literal: In spring of year twelve he went out as Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year's spring he went out as Wuxing administrator.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人黃睦之家居烏程，子弟專橫，前太守皆折節事之。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentleman Huang Muzhi's family lived in Wucheng; his sons and nephews were overbearing, and former administrators all bent the knee to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat gentleman Huang Muzhi's house was in Wucheng; his kin bullied the circuit, and every prior administrator bowed to them.

sentences.zh: 覽未到郡，睦之子弟來迎，覽逐去其船，杖吏爲通者。

translations.literal: Before Lan reached the commandery, Muzhi's kin came to welcome him; Lan drove off their boats and beat the clerks who had cleared the way for them.
translations.idiomatic: Before Lan arrived, Muzhi's kin came to meet him; he drove off their boats and whipped the clerks who had let them through.

sentences.zh: 自是睦之家杜門不出，不敢與公私關通。

translations.literal: From then on Muzhi's household shut their doors and did not venture out, daring no private or official dealings.
translations.idiomatic: After that Muzhi's clan stayed indoors and dared no public or private traffic.

sentences.zh: 郡境多劫，爲東道患，覽下車肅然，一境清謐。

translations.literal: The commandery had many robbers and was a scourge on the eastern route; when Lan took his carriage down the district grew stern and the whole region grew quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Robbery was rife and troubled the eastern roads; when Lan took office the whole district grew orderly and still.

sentences.zh: 初，齊明帝及覽父綍、東海徐孝嗣，並爲吳興，號稱名守，覽皆欲過之！

translations.literal: Earlier Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Di, and Xu Xiaosi of Donghai had all governed Wuxing and been called famed administrators—Lan wished to surpass them all!
translations.idiomatic: Once Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Di, and Donghai's Xu Xiaosi had all ruled Wuxing as famed administrators—Lan meant to outdo them all!

sentences.zh: 昔覽在新安頗聚斂，至是遂稱廉潔，時人方之王懷祖。

translations.literal: Long ago in Xin'an Lan had greatly gathered wealth; now he was praised as pure and clean, and men compared him to Wang Huainzu.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Xin'an he had been grasping; now he was called incorrupt, and the age compared him to Wang Huainzu.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，時年三十七。

translations.literal: He died in office at age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 詔贈中書令。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace library director.

sentences.zh: 子罕，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Han died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han died early.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：謝朏之於宋代，蓋忠義者歟？

translations.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: In the Song age, was Xie Fei perhaps a man of loyalty and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Was Xie Fei, in Song times, a man of loyalty and righteousness?

sentences.zh: 當齊建武之世，拂衣止足，永元多難，確然獨善，其疏、蔣之流乎。

translations.literal: In Qi Jianwu times he folded his robe and checked his step; in Yongyuan's many troubles he stood firm in doing good alone—is he not of the sort of Shu and Jiang?
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Jianwu he held back his robes; amid Yongyuan's troubles he stood alone in the good—one of Shu and Jiang's kind?

sentences.zh: 洎高祖龍興，旁求物色，角巾來仕，首陟台司，極出處之致矣！

translations.literal: When Gaozu's dragon fortune rose, he sought men on every hand; Fei came to serve in scholar's kerchief and first climbed the terraces of state—he had reached the utmost of entering and leaving office!
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose, he searched widely; Fei came in plain kerchief and first reached the high ministries—the full arc of public life!

sentences.zh: 覽終能善政，君子韙之。

translations.literal: Lan in the end could govern well; gentlemen approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Lan could govern well to the end; gentlemen praised it.

translations.literal: [1] Editorial footnote marker in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Editorial footnote marker.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七三年五月版《梁書》爲本校。

translations.idiomatic: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang (May 1973).
